result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A puts orders and revenue in separate, aligned panels on the same month layout. Each panel has its own heading and unit, so neither series can be misread against the other. B overlays revenue on orders with two independent y-axes, so where the line crosses or sits above a bar depends only on the scales chosen. B also names its series only in a legend, and neither screenshot shows an observation about how the two series relate. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B puts orders and revenue in separate aligned panels on a shared month axis. Each panel has a clear heading and unit, and both bar charts start at zero. A uses a dual-axis bar and line overlay, so where the line and bars meet depends only on how the two scales were picked, which is the setup the rubric warns against. Neither screenshot shows an explicit note on what the two series show together; B's average-order-value card comes closest.
